question_text: Which of the following inputs is SAFE to paste directly into a non-approved external AI tool when preparing a client briefing?
scenario_text: You are preparing a briefing note for an upcoming review meeting with Crestwood Logistics Pty Ltd. You have access to their latest audited financials, an internal risk rating of 'Watch', a draft term sheet, and a publicly available industry report on freight logistics trends. You want to use an AI tool to help structure the briefing quickly.

options.label: A
options.text: The publicly available industry report on freight logistics trends, with no client-specific details added.

options.label: B
options.text: The client's audited financial statements, since they are already signed off and filed.

options.label: C
options.text: The internal risk rating note, because it is only one line of text and unlikely to cause harm.

options.label: D
options.text: The draft term sheet, because it has not yet been executed and is therefore not a final document.

question_text: The prompt below was used to prepare for a client renewal conversation but produced a vague, unhelpful response. Diagnose the prompting weaknesses and rewrite it as a stronger prompt that would generate a more useful output for an RM.
scenario_text:
An RM used this prompt before a facility renewal meeting:

'Help me prepare for a meeting with a client about renewing their loan.'

The AI returned a generic list of 'tips for client meetings' that was not useful for the RM's specific situation. The client is a mid-market construction company with a $3M working capital facility up for annual review. The RM wants to anticipate objections, identify upsell opportunities, and prepare 3 tailored talking points about the value the bank has delivered over the past year.

criteria.name: Diagnosis of prompt weaknesses
criteria.description: Learner correctly identifies at least two specific weaknesses: missing role/persona, no sector or client context, no specific output requested, and no constraints on format or purpose.

criteria.name: Quality of rewritten prompt
criteria.description: The rewritten prompt includes: a role frame (RM preparing for renewal), abstracted client context (mid-market construction, working capital facility), specific outputs requested (objection anticipation, upsell opportunities, value talking points), and a clear format instruction.

question_text: An AI tool drafts the following sentence for inclusion in a credit memo: 'Vantara Foods has consistently demonstrated strong liquidity management, with a current ratio well above industry benchmarks.' What is the most important critical evaluation step before including this in the memo?
scenario_text: You used an approved AI tool to help draft sections of a credit memo for Vantara Foods (a fictional client). The AI generated the sentence above based on your abstracted prompt describing the client as a 'food manufacturer with stable working capital.' You are about to paste it into the memo for submission to the credit committee.

options.label: A
options.text: Verify the claim against the client's actual financial data — confirm the current ratio figure and check it against a credible industry benchmark before including it.

options.label: B
options.text: Check that the sentence is grammatically correct and professionally worded before pasting it in.

options.label: C
options.text: Ask the AI to regenerate the sentence with more specific language to make it sound more authoritative.

options.label: D
options.text: Accept the sentence as accurate because it matches the general description you provided in your prompt.

question_text: An AI tool produced the portfolio insight summary below. Evaluate the quality of the data reasoning and identify any decisions an RM should NOT make based solely on this output, explaining why.
scenario_text:
AI-generated portfolio insight summary:

'Analysis of your portfolio indicates that clients in the retail sector are your lowest-performing segment by revenue contribution. These clients have the highest average cost-to-serve and the lowest product cross-sell ratio. Based on this, it is recommended that you deprioritise retail clients in your outreach plan and focus resources on manufacturing and logistics clients, who show stronger revenue metrics and higher facility utilisation.'

Your task: (1) Identify at least two data reasoning problems or missing considerations in this analysis. (2) Explain what decisions an RM should not make based solely on this AI output, and why.

criteria.name: Identification of data reasoning gaps
criteria.description: Learner identifies at least two specific gaps: e.g., the analysis ignores strategic value of retail relationships (referrals, tenure, growth potential), does not account for individual client variation within the segment, and may be based on incomplete or point-in-time data.

criteria.name: Decisions the RM should not make solely on this output
criteria.description: Learner correctly identifies that the RM should not deprioritise or reduce service to retail clients, reallocate portfolio resources, or make any client-facing decisions based solely on this AI summary — and explains that such decisions require human judgement, relationship context, and management input.

question_text: An RM wants to use AI to prepare a client intelligence summary before an annual review meeting. Which approach best demonstrates effective use of AI for relationship intelligence while staying within responsible AI boundaries?
scenario_text: You have an annual review meeting next week with the CEO of Driftwood Packaging Co., a long-standing client. You want to walk in with a sharp understanding of their business context, recent industry developments, and potential needs. You have access to publicly available news, the company's published annual report, and your own (sanitised) notes from previous meetings.

options.label: A
options.text: Prompt the AI with publicly available information (industry news, published annual report excerpts, sector trends) and your sanitised meeting notes to generate a structured pre-meeting intelligence brief covering business context, likely priorities, and suggested conversation angles.

options.label: B
options.text: Paste the client's full CRM record including internal risk ratings and deal history into the AI tool to get the most comprehensive intelligence summary possible.

options.label: C
options.text: Ask the AI to generate a client profile from scratch using only the company name, since AI tools have access to up-to-date business databases.

options.label: D
options.text: Use the AI to write a summary of the client's financial performance based on figures you recall from internal credit reports, without checking the source.

question_text: An RM uses AI to draft a follow-up email to a client after a difficult conversation about a declined credit application. Which of the following best describes the correct approach to using the AI draft?
scenario_text: You had a tense call with the CFO of Irongate Civil Pty Ltd after their facility increase request was declined by the credit committee. You want to send a professional, empathetic follow-up email that acknowledges their disappointment, explains the next steps, and keeps the relationship intact. You use an approved AI tool to draft the email.

options.label: A
options.text: Review the AI draft carefully, adjust the tone to reflect your genuine relationship with the CFO, verify that all stated next steps are accurate, and ensure no confidential credit committee reasoning is inadvertently disclosed before sending.

options.label: B
options.text: Send the AI draft immediately — it will be more professionally worded than anything you could write quickly, and speed matters after a difficult conversation.

options.label: C
options.text: Ask the AI to make the email more persuasive so the client feels the decision was the right one, without changing any factual content.

options.label: D
options.text: Use the AI draft as the final version but add the client's name and your signature, since personalisation is sufficient review for a routine follow-up.

question_text: Which of the following inputs is safe to include verbatim in an EDC-approved AI tool prompt without any abstraction or modification?
scenario_text: You are an Underwriter preparing a risk summary for a new transaction involving Thornfield Agri-Export Inc. You have four documents available: an internal CIS buyer-file note with payment history and risk commentary, a publicly available trade credit rating report published by a recognised ratings agency, a draft term sheet with proposed covenant thresholds, and an internal memo showing the deal's preliminary risk rating and rationale. You want to use an EDC-approved AI tool to help structure your analysis.

options.label: A
options.text: The publicly available trade credit rating report sourced from the ratings agency's published website.

options.label: B
options.text: The internal CIS buyer-file note, because it is stored on EDC's secure internal system.

options.label: C
options.text: The draft term sheet, because the deal has not yet been approved and no client has signed it.

options.label: D
options.text: The internal risk rating memo, because it contains analytical reasoning rather than raw financial figures.

question_text: Review the prompt below, which an Underwriter used to draft a covenant analysis section. Identify at least two specific structural weaknesses that reduce the quality of the AI output, and rewrite the prompt to address those weaknesses.
scenario_text:
An Underwriter submitted the following prompt to an EDC-approved AI tool:

---
"Analyse the covenants for this deal and tell me if they are appropriate."
---

The AI returned a two-sentence response stating that covenants are generally important for credit risk management and that leverage and interest coverage ratios are commonly used. The Underwriter found this unhelpful. Diagnose the prompt's weaknesses and produce an improved version.

criteria.name: Diagnosis of prompt weaknesses
criteria.description: Identifies at least two specific structural weaknesses: e.g., no context about the borrower or transaction type, no definition of 'appropriate,' no output format specified, no analytical criteria provided, no role framing, and no abstracted inputs supplied to ground the analysis.

criteria.name: Quality of rewritten prompt
criteria.description: The rewritten prompt includes role framing or context, specifies the type of transaction and borrower profile (abstracted), defines what 'appropriate' means in underwriting terms (e.g., aligned with leverage profile, sector norms), requests a structured output, and includes a constraint on handling missing information.

question_text: An AI tool has generated a financial risk summary for a borrower in the renewable energy sector. Which of the following responses represents the most appropriate underwriter behaviour when reviewing this output before including it in a credit paper?
scenario_text: You used an EDC-approved AI tool to draft the 'Financial Risk' section of a credit paper for a solar project developer. The AI output states: 'The borrower's debt service coverage ratio of 1.35x is within acceptable range for project finance transactions in this sector, and the leverage profile is consistent with investment-grade issuers.' You do not recall providing the DSCR figure in your prompt, and you know the borrower's actual leverage is higher than investment-grade norms.

options.label: A
options.text: Verify the DSCR figure against the source financial model, correct the leverage characterisation based on your own analysis, and revise the section before including it in the credit paper.

options.label: B
options.text: Accept the output as a reasonable approximation since AI tools are trained on large datasets and sector benchmarks are likely accurate.

options.label: C
options.text: Delete only the leverage sentence and keep the DSCR statement, since one error does not invalidate the rest of the AI-generated content.

options.label: D
options.text: Flag the section as 'AI-generated' in the credit paper so reviewers know to apply their own judgement, without making any changes yourself.

question_text: Review the AI-generated analysis excerpt below, which was produced to support a credit decision. Identify at least two analytical weaknesses or data reasoning errors that an Underwriter should correct before relying on this output, and explain what additional analysis or data would be needed.
scenario_text:
An Underwriter used an EDC-approved AI tool to analyse an abstracted borrower profile. The AI produced the following excerpt for the 'Financial Assessment' section:

---
"The borrower's revenue has grown at an average of 12% per year over the past three years, indicating strong business momentum. The current ratio of 1.8x suggests adequate short-term liquidity. Based on these indicators, the borrower demonstrates a solid financial profile consistent with investment-grade characteristics. The debt service coverage ratio is not provided but is assumed to be sufficient given the revenue growth trend."
---

criteria.name: Identification of analytical weaknesses
criteria.description: Identifies at least two specific analytical weaknesses: e.g., revenue growth alone does not indicate creditworthiness without profitability or margin data; 'investment-grade' characterisation is unsupported by the data provided; the DSCR assumption is a hallucinated inference not grounded in any provided figure; the current ratio alone is insufficient to assess liquidity without context on payables, inventory quality, or cash position.

criteria.name: Additional analysis or data requirements
criteria.description: Identifies what additional data or analysis is needed: e.g., actual DSCR from the financial model, EBITDA margin and net income trends, leverage ratio, cash flow from operations, and sector benchmarks to contextualise the current ratio and growth rate before any creditworthiness conclusion can be drawn.

question_text: An Underwriter is preparing for a first meeting with a new financial institution partner to discuss a potential risk-sharing arrangement. Which use of AI is most appropriate for building relationship intelligence ahead of this meeting?
scenario_text: You are an Underwriter preparing for an introductory meeting with Meridian Trade Finance Bank, a regional bank seeking to co-insure a portfolio of export receivables. You have access to the bank's publicly available annual report, a press release about their recent trade finance expansion, and an internal briefing note from the deal team. You want to use AI to help you prepare.

options.label: A
options.text: Use an EDC-approved AI tool to synthesise publicly available information about the bank's trade finance strategy, recent announcements, and regional focus to prepare informed questions and identify potential alignment with EDC's mandate.

options.label: B
options.text: Paste the internal deal team briefing note into a general AI chatbot to generate a relationship summary, since the note contains the most relevant context for the meeting.

options.label: C
options.text: Ask the AI to predict the bank's risk appetite and likely negotiating positions based on their public profile, and treat the output as a reliable basis for your meeting strategy.

options.label: D
options.text: Use AI to draft a relationship history summary by asking it to recall previous EDC interactions with Meridian Trade Finance Bank from its training data.

question_text: An Underwriter has used an AI tool to draft a section of a credit paper. Which of the following practices best reflects responsible and effective use of AI-augmented communication in this context?
scenario_text: You have used an EDC-approved AI tool to draft the 'Transaction Overview' section of a credit paper for a structured trade finance deal. The AI-generated draft is well-written and covers the main structural elements. However, you notice it uses generic language about the guarantee structure that does not accurately reflect the specific risk-sharing arrangement in this deal, and it omits the rationale for EDC's involvement.

options.label: A
options.text: Edit the draft to correct the guarantee structure description, add the EDC mandate rationale, verify all factual claims, and ensure the final section reflects your professional judgement before submitting.

options.label: B
options.text: Submit the AI draft as written since it is well-structured and the approval committee will identify any inaccuracies during their review.

options.label: C
options.text: Add a footnote stating 'drafted with AI assistance' and submit without changes, as disclosure of AI use satisfies the quality assurance requirement.

options.label: D
options.text: Ask the AI to revise the section by providing the correct guarantee structure details, including the specific deal terms, to get a more accurate draft.

question_text: Which of the following inputs is safe to include verbatim in a Copilot prompt without any abstraction or modification?
scenario_text: You are an Analyst preparing a sector overview for a client briefing. You have several documents on your desk: an internal credit risk rating memo for a corporate client, a published annual report from a publicly listed company, a draft strategy document from your team, and a third-party embargoed research report. You need to use Copilot to help synthesise background information.

options.label: A
options.text: The published annual report of the publicly listed company, sourced from its investor relations website.

options.label: B
options.text: The internal credit risk rating memo, because it is already stored in your organisation's secure drive.

options.label: C
options.text: The embargoed third-party research report, because it contains sector-level data rather than client-specific data.

options.label: D
options.text: The draft strategy document, because it has not yet been formally classified as confidential.

question_text: Review the Copilot prompt below. Identify its weaknesses as a strategic prompt, then rewrite it to be significantly more effective for the analyst's stated purpose.
scenario_text:
An Analyst at Northgate Advisory submitted this Copilot prompt to help prepare for a client meeting:

---
"Tell me about the mining sector."
---

The analyst's actual goal was to prepare a five-minute verbal briefing for a relationship manager who is meeting a mid-sized copper mining company to discuss potential export financing. The briefing should cover current commodity price trends, key operational risks, and one or two talking points relevant to export financing conversations.

criteria.name: Weakness diagnosis
criteria.description: Correctly identifies at least two weaknesses in the original prompt: it is too broad/vague, specifies no audience or purpose, defines no output format, and provides no analytical focus or scope.

criteria.name: Role and context added
criteria.description: The rewritten prompt specifies a role for Copilot and provides relevant context (e.g., preparing a verbal briefing for a relationship manager meeting a copper mining company to discuss export financing).

criteria.name: Format and scope defined
criteria.description: The rewritten prompt specifies the output format (e.g., a concise verbal briefing outline or bullet points) and scope (e.g., commodity price trends, operational risks, export financing talking points).

criteria.name: Overall improvement in strategic quality
criteria.description: The rewritten prompt is substantially more likely to produce a useful, targeted output than the original — it is specific, purposeful, and calibrated to the analyst's actual workflow need.

question_text: An Analyst uses Copilot to generate a summary of financial risk indicators for a sector report. Which action best reflects critical evaluation of the AI output before it is used in a client-facing document?
scenario_text: You are an Analyst at Harlow Financial Group. You used Copilot to generate a paragraph summarising key financial risk indicators for the commercial real estate sector. The output reads fluently and cites what appear to be specific statistics (e.g., 'vacancy rates rose to 18.4% in Q2' and 'debt-service coverage ratios fell below 1.2x for 34% of loans'). You are about to paste this paragraph into a sector briefing note that will be shared with clients.

options.label: A
options.text: Verify the specific statistics against the original source documents or authoritative databases before including them, and flag any figures that cannot be confirmed.

options.label: B
options.text: Accept the output as accurate because Copilot is connected to organisational data and would not fabricate statistics.

options.label: C
options.text: Lightly edit the paragraph for tone and include it, since the figures are plausible and consistent with general market knowledge.

options.label: D
options.text: Ask Copilot to regenerate the paragraph twice more and use the version that appears most consistent across the three outputs.

question_text: Review the AI-generated data interpretation below. Identify any analytical errors, unsupported conclusions, or data reasoning problems, and explain what the analyst should do before using this output in a portfolio review.
scenario_text:
An Analyst asked Copilot to analyse five years of EBITDA margin data for 40 industrial manufacturers. Copilot returned the following interpretation:

---
'Analysis of the dataset shows that EBITDA margins across the sector have improved steadily by an average of 2.3 percentage points per year over the five-year period. This confirms that the industrial manufacturing sector is in a strong growth phase and presents low credit risk overall. Three companies — Ferrotek Industries, Caldwell Precision, and Morrow Components — show margins significantly below the sector average and should be immediately flagged as high credit risk and removed from the portfolio. The trend is consistent and unlikely to reverse given current macroeconomic conditions.'
---

Your task: Identify all analytical and reasoning problems in this output, and specify what steps the analyst should take before acting on these findings.

criteria.name: Analytical errors identified
criteria.description: Identifies at least two analytical errors: (1) conflating EBITDA margin improvement with 'low credit risk overall' — margin is one indicator, not a complete credit assessment; (2) the conclusion that below-average margin alone justifies 'high credit risk' and immediate portfolio removal is an unsupported leap; (3) the forward-looking claim about macroeconomic conditions is speculative and unsourced.

criteria.name: Reasoning problems flagged
criteria.description: Flags that Copilot has made a definitive recommendation (remove companies from portfolio) that exceeds its appropriate role — AI should surface patterns for analyst review, not make portfolio decisions — and that the output presents speculation as certainty.

criteria.name: Corrective analyst steps specified
criteria.description: Specifies at least two concrete steps the analyst should take before acting: e.g., verify the 2.3pp average figure against the raw data, conduct a fuller credit assessment of the three flagged companies using multiple indicators, and treat the macroeconomic claim as unverified.

question_text: An Analyst is asked to use AI to help prepare a relationship intelligence briefing ahead of a client meeting. Which approach best demonstrates responsible and effective use of AI for this task?
scenario_text: You are an Analyst at Harlow Financial Group supporting a relationship manager who has a first meeting next week with Solaris Packaging Inc., a mid-sized manufacturer. The relationship manager wants a briefing note covering the company's recent business developments, key decision-makers, and any publicly known strategic priorities. You have access to Copilot and a range of public sources.

options.label: A
options.text: Use Copilot to synthesise publicly available information (press releases, news articles, published financials) into a structured briefing note, then verify key facts and add analyst commentary before sharing with the relationship manager.

options.label: B
options.text: Export the client's CRM interaction history and financial exposure data into Copilot to generate a comprehensive briefing that includes internal relationship notes.

options.label: C
options.text: Ask Copilot to generate a full briefing note from memory without providing any source documents, since it has broad knowledge of business and industry.

options.label: D
options.text: Use Copilot only to format and proofread a briefing note you have already written manually, since AI should not be involved in relationship intelligence tasks.

question_text: An Analyst uses Copilot to draft a client-facing briefing note. Which approach best reflects responsible and effective use of AI for professional communication?
scenario_text: You are an Analyst at Northgate Advisory. Your director has asked you to produce a two-page briefing note for a corporate client summarising recent developments in the global shipping and logistics sector. You use Copilot to generate a first draft based on publicly available sources. The draft is well-structured and reads fluently, but you have not yet reviewed it in detail.

options.label: A
options.text: Review the draft carefully for factual accuracy, tone appropriateness, and any claims that need verification or caveating, then edit and personalise it before sending to the client.

options.label: B
options.text: Send the Copilot draft directly to the client, since it is based on public sources and reads professionally.

options.label: C
options.text: Ask Copilot to review its own draft for errors and send the revised version without further analyst review.

options.label: D
options.text: Discard the Copilot draft and write the briefing note entirely from scratch to ensure full ownership of the content.
